requirements.quote:
The shared database holds domain space data for the local name server
and resolver.
requirements.condition: When the local name server and resolver use the described shared-database configuration.
requirements.required_behavior: The shared database holds domain-space data for both the local name server and the resolver.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected configuration can be inspected to establish that both components obtain domain-space data from the shared database.

requirements.quote:
The structure of the domain data and the necessity for
synchronization between name servers and resolvers imply the general
characteristics of this database, but the actual format is up to the
local implementor.
requirements.condition: When implementing the shared database for the local name server and resolver.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementor may choose the actual format of the shared database.
requirements.why_checkable: The database representation is an inspectable implementation choice; this permission does not require a particular representation.

requirements.required_behavior: Synchronize the domain data used by the name server and resolver.
requirements.why_checkable: The passage mentions a necessity for synchronization but does not specify its invariant, timing, or mechanism; it does not support a definite implementation check in this chunk.

requirements.quote:
Information flow can also be tailored so that a group of hosts act
together to optimize activities.  Sometimes this is done to offload less
capable hosts so that they do not have to implement a full resolver.
This can be appropriate for PCs or hosts which want to minimize the
amount of new network code which is required.  This scheme can also
allow a group of hosts can share a small number of caches rather than
maintaining a large number of separate caches, on the premise that the
centralized caches will have a higher hit ratio.  In either case,
resolvers are replaced with stub resolvers which act as front ends to
resolvers located in a recursive server in one or more name servers
known to perform that service:
requirements.condition: When a group of hosts uses the described resolver-offloading configuration.
requirements.required_behavior: A host may use a stub resolver backed by a recursive server instead of implementing a full resolver locally.
requirements.why_checkable: The host resolver role and its use of a remote recursive service can be inspected; choosing this configuration is optional.

requirements.quote:
Information flow can also be tailored so that a group of hosts act
together to optimize activities.  Sometimes this is done to offload less
capable hosts so that they do not have to implement a full resolver.
This can be appropriate for PCs or hosts which want to minimize the
amount of new network code which is required.  This scheme can also
allow a group of hosts can share a small number of caches rather than
maintaining a large number of separate caches, on the premise that the
centralized caches will have a higher hit ratio.  In either case,
resolvers are replaced with stub resolvers which act as front ends to
resolvers located in a recursive server in one or more name servers
known to perform that service:

                   Local Hosts                     |  Foreign
                                                   |
    +---------+                                    |
    |         | responses                          |
    | Stub    |<--------------------+              |
    | Resolver|                     |              |
    |         |----------------+    |              |
    +---------+ recursive      |    |              |
                queries        |    |              |
                               V    |              |
    +---------+ recursive     +----------+         |  +--------+
    |         | queries       |          |queries  |  |        |
    | Stub    |-------------->| Recursive|---------|->|Foreign |
    | Resolver|               | Server   |         |  |  Name  |
    |         |<--------------|          |<--------|--| Server |
    +---------+ responses     |          |responses|  |        |
                              +----------+         |  +--------+
                              |  Central |         |
                              |   cache  |         |
                              +----------+         |
requirements.condition: When using the illustrated stub-resolver and recursive-server configuration.
requirements.required_behavior: The stub resolver sends recursive queries to the recursive server.
requirements.why_checkable: Queries emitted by the stub can be captured to check that they request recursion and are sent to the configured recursive server.

requirements.quote:
In any case, note that domain components are always replicated for
reliability whenever possible.
requirements.condition: Whenever replication of domain components is possible.
requirements.required_behavior: Replicate domain components for reliability whenever possible.
requirements.why_checkable: Replication can be observed, but this chunk does not define which domain components are covered or how feasibility is determined, so the applicability is insufficient for a definite implementation check.
